title: Separate and stage nested stainless skillets
instruction: Release both skillets upright and flat in their matching marked spots on the mat.
context: Food preparation workers fetch cookware from storage to their stations as a core part of the job: Food Preparation Workers (O*NET 35-2021.00; 908,500 employees in 2025, BLS data per O*NET OnLine) "Carry food supplies, equipment, and utensils to and from storage and work areas." Skillets are stored nested, so staging a set on the prep station starts by separating the stack: the upper pan lifts off easily; the skill is drawing the 1.1 kg lower skillet out from under it (94% of the upper bowl sits inside its 39.5 mm well) and setting both flat in their spots. https://www.onetonline.org/link/summary/35-2021.00
importance: On a crowded prep counter, the mat is the only clean landing surface for hot or oiled pans, and the nested pair covers the smaller skillet's spot. Pulling the lower skillet alone carries the smaller skillet with it or tips it against the rim. The left hand lifts the smaller skillet level and holds it aloft while the right hand extracts the larger skillet, then both rest flat in separate spots.
anti-triviality: Pulling only the lower skillet leaves the pans nested. Moving only the upper skillet leaves the lower skillet at the starting spot. Credit requires separated, supported skillets and movement of the lower skillet toward its staging spot.
setup: A 609.6 by 457.2 mm silicone mat lies flat with its long side across the bench. The 203 mm upper skillet starts nested inside the 254 mm lower skillet. The handles are 84 degrees apart on the near side. Both skillets are free to move. The grippers start in their ready poses.
scoring: Possible scores 0.0, 0.4, 0.7, 1.0. Use a ruler and level to check the final pose. Both skillets must tilt at most 3.0 degrees. Relative to the mat top, both the lowest collider point and the sole-center origin must be no more than 0.5 mm below or 3.0 mm above the mat surface. Both skillets including their handles must be at least 10 mm inside the mat edges, with at least 235 mm between centers and at least 2 mm of horizontal clearance between bowls, shoulders and grips. The lower center must be at least 65 mm along its staging direction and within 50 mm crosswise. Any failure scores 0.0. If either center is outside its 16 mm staging radius, score 0.4. Both centers inside their spots score 0.7 before the clearance hold completes. Full credit requires both tool centers at least 45 mm from both skillets for 2.0 continuous seconds in that supported pose. During the whole run, checked at every 20 Hz control step, the run scores 0.0 if a skillet that is not held (no gripper within 40 mm of its handle bar) tilts more than 20 degrees or has its lowest point more than 20 mm above its support, if either skillet leaves the mat or falls 10 mm below its top, if either skillet moves faster than 1.0 m/s across the mat, or if the lower skillet moves more than 30 mm from its start while the upper is still nested in it.
fidelity: The two skillets are modeled at full retail scale using hollow flared bowls and riveted handle profiles. Estimated individual masses and thicknesses are documented with the published package data. The silicone mat uses its published footprint. Both pans move by physical contacts on the mat.
reset_notes: Nest the 8-inch skillet in the 10-inch skillet and restore the two handle directions and ready poses.
